issue.title: Proxied compressed EOF framed message never completes

milestone.title: release-1.5.0
milestone.description:
A little over 6 months in the making, Ratpack 1.5.0 is now available. 
This release adds many new features and capabilities, squashes copious bugs and refines and optimizes many internals. 
Ratpack 1.5.0 is bigger, badder and faster.

The following core dependencies have been upgraded:

* Jackson 2.7.5 → 2.8.7
* Netty 4.1.4.Final → 4.1.9.Final
* Guava 19.0 → 21.0
* Caffeine 2.3.1 → 2.4.0
* Slf4j 1.7.21 → 1.7.28

The new `ratpack-jdbc-tx` module adds support for `Promise` based JDBC transactions.
It centers around the new [`ratpack.jdbctx.Transaction`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/jdbctx/Transaction.html) type.

The new `ratpack-consul` modules provides the [`ratpack.consul.RatpackConsulConfig`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/consul/RatpackConsulConfig.htm)
factory for creating configuration sources backed by [Consul](https://www.consul.io/). 
This is a convenient way to centralize configuration for your app and separate it from deployment.

The new [`Promise.mapIf`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Promise.html#mapIf-ratpack.func.Predicate-ratpack.func.Function-ratpack.func.Function-) 
and [`Promise.flatMapIf`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Promise.html#flatMapIf-ratpack.func.Predicate-ratpack.func.Function-ratpack.func.Function-)
methods allowing supplying an “else” to a promise transform.

The new [`Promise.retry`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Promise.html#retry-int-java.time.Duration-ratpack.func.BiAction-) methods allowing retrying a failed promise with various strategies.

The new [`Promise.defer`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Promise.html#defer-java.time.Duration-) methods make it more convenient to delay yielding a promise.

The new [`Promise.cacheResultFor`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Promise.html#cacheResultFor-ratpack.func.Function-) method (and friends)
make it easier to have more sophisticated caching policies for async values.

The new [`Promise.close`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Promise.html#close-ratpack.exec.Operation-) method makes it easier
to perform async cleanup/disposal.

Various new utilities have been added to the `Streams` class such as 
[`fork()`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/stream/Streams.html#fork-org.reactivestreams.Publisher-ratpack.func.Action-ratpack.func.Action-),
[`take()`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/stream/Streams.html#take-long-org.reactivestreams.Publisher-),
[`concat()`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/stream/Streams.html#concat-java.lang.Iterable-),
[`batch()`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/stream/Streams.html#batch-int-org.reactivestreams.Publisher-ratpack.func.Action-)
and [`flatten()`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/stream/Streams.html#flatten-org.reactivestreams.Publisher-ratpack.func.Action-).
These utilities enable more patterns for working with async data streams.

The new [`ByteBufStreams`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/stream/bytebuf/ByteBufStreams.html) 
class provides utilities for dealing with streams of Netty `ByteBuf`.

The new [`Execution.sleep()`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/Execution.html#sleep-java.time.Duration-ratpack.func.Block-) 
methods provide a non blocking analog to `Thread.sleep()`.

You can now specify an [idle timeout](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/server/ServerConfigBuilder.html#idleTimeout-java.time.Duration-) 
for server connections. This affects active connections and inactive connections (i.e. keepalive).
It can also be [overridden on a per request basis](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/http/Request.html#setIdleTimeout-java.time.Duration-),
which is particularly useful when streaming a lot of data, or streaming eternally.

Ratpack's HTTP client now supports SSL connections leveraging SNI. No extra config is required.

The new [`ReadWriteAccess`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/exec/util/ReadWriteAccess.html) 
utility is an analog of the JDK's [`ReadWriteLock`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/locks/ReadWriteLock.html).

The new [`FileIo`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/file/FileIo.html) utility provides non blocking filesystem read/write access.

It is now possible to use Netty's SSL support via [ServerConfigBuilder.ssl](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/server/ServerConfigBuilder.html#ssl-io.netty.handler.ssl.SslContext-).
Netty's SSL implementation is far more efficient in environments where OpenSSL is available.
All users currently using SSL with Ratpack should migrate to using this new method.

If the client connecting to the server identified itself, you can now obtain its certificate via [`Request.getClientCertificate`](https://ratpack.io/manual/1.5.0/api/ratpack/http/Request.html#getClientCertificate--).

There are also many other new convenience methods, bug fixes and generally cool stuff added in this release.
Thanks to all who contributed.

We hope you enjoy Ratpack 1.5.

-- 

**Team Ratpack**

body: I've just confirmed that this issue isn't present with 4.1.1.
@alkemist sounds correct... Want to create a PR for it ?

@alkemist actually can you confirm this is really caused by the commit you listed here ? I am a bit confused as you say you see a `PrematureChannelClosureException` which would be caused by the `HttpRequestDecoder` that sit in front of the `HttpContentDecoder` so what you do in `HttpContentDecoder` should have no impact here. Or do you think it happens because its used as proxy and so modify the stuff in between?
@alkemist no worries I think I have an idea how to easily fix it and write a test. stay tuned...
Great. Can you please let me know if this isn't going to make it into a release soon. If it isn't, I'll have to patch around it on my end.
@alkemist hopefully I can fit this in before I cut the release this week.
@normanmaurer I hate to be that guy, but… any update on this? :)
